reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an instructional AdMob/AdSense walkthrough covering account creation, app ad placement, verification, ad-unit configuration, and payment setup. The per-click earnings and withdrawal threshold are framed as explanations within that advertising tutorial, while the like/subscribe request is ordinary channel engagement rather than a payment condition.

citations.quote: In this video I'm going to tell you How to earn online services
create applications where we will put ads Which will help us to earn
follow this video and create an account
After that we just create our AdSense account here
Now let's create 2 ads First one is Banner Ad

opening.argument: Judge, this is more than a neutral explanation of advertising. The speaker connects an income promise to a sequence the viewer is urged to follow: make applications and place ads, then create the accounts needed to pursue those earnings. The appeal becomes sharper when the speaker describes substantial returns from a single ad click. The issue is not whether an AdMob account can be created; it is whether the video uses the prospect of easy income to move viewers into an account-creation flow.

citations.quote: create applications where we will put ads Which will help us to earn
So guys, follow this video and create an account
both these account are importants for you earnings
Click one time to earn big money

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's account-creation and banner-ad quotes establish that the video demonstrates a workflow, but they do not settle how that workflow is sold to viewers. The speaker expressly says following the video and creating an account leads into making and earning, then highlights money from a click. Instructional steps can also be the mechanism of an income solicitation.

citations.quote: So guys, follow this video and create an account And the work i'll tell you later you gotta start making and earning your video
After 1 click,it gives you $0.015-$3

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted steps concern creating apps and configuring advertising accounts, not claiming a free payment for signing up. The video shows the viewer how to create ad units and says a later installment will cover making applications and putting ads in them. Its loose per-click claim does not convert that operational demonstration into a promised withdrawal from an account-creation action.

citations.quote: Now let's create 2 ads First one is Banner Ad
in next part i'll show how you could create your applications and how you can put ads in all those applications

opening.argument: Consider the signals together: the speaker says one click can earn big money, cites a higher per-click amount heard from others, and discusses a withdrawal threshold. Alongside those claims, viewers are walked through supplying identity and address details for payment setup. None of those details alone proves abuse. Together, though, they make the earnings pitch consequential: an attractive but unverified return is paired with steps involving personal information and the expectation of a later payout.

citations.quote: Click one time to earn big money
I heard that after clicking on ads,they got more then $5
Set payment method. And you just need to fill the details here you have to add your address Your id card should be fully specified when you add it.
As soon as 100$ are completed you will be able to make withdrawal here

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the figures explanations within a tutorial, but the wording matters: 'big money' from one click is an inducement, not just a menu-setting instruction. The defense's examples of account and ad-unit creation do not verify the cited return or show that a viewer following the steps will reach the stated withdrawal threshold.

citations.quote: Click one time to earn big money
As soon as 100$ are completed you will be able to make withdrawal here

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The figures deserve skepticism, especially where the speaker says a higher amount is something he heard. But the cited payment details appear in a walkthrough of an AdMob Payments page, and the video also shows an ad unit being created. The prosecution has identified questionable earnings language, not evidence that viewers are directed to surrender information to the speaker or promised cash merely for completing these steps.

citations.quote: I heard that after clicking on ads,they got more then $5

opening.argument: The tutorial format should not obscure the video's promotional purpose. Its title leads with earning money, the description ties wanting to earn more online to subscribing and liking, and the speaker calls application-based earning the best way to make money before urging viewers to follow the video and create an account. Those are participation prompts wrapped around the demonstration. A judge should assess the combined pitch, not isolate the on-screen account steps from the income appeal that brings viewers to them.

citations.quote: Earn money with google adsense fully Activated - App Earning Part 1
if you want to more earn $$$ online then subscribe my chanal and like this video
So today the best way to earn money is application based one.
So guys, follow this video and create an account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense separates the like-and-subscribe request from the money discussion, yet the description explicitly puts them in the same appeal. And while the walkthrough covers real configuration steps, that does not erase the opening claim that application-based earning is the best way to make money. The educational presentation also serves to recruit viewers into the proposed earning activity.

citations.quote: if you want to more earn $$$ online then subscribe my chanal and like this video
So today the best way to earn money is application based one.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and instruction can coexist. The description asks for ordinary channel engagement, but it does not say subscribing produces earnings. The substantive demonstration concerns signing up for AdMob, adding an app, and creating ads; the speaker says a later part will show application creation and ad placement. Calling that activity an opportunity to earn does not by itself establish a deceptive reward offer.
